messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: exp(linear predictor) as a covariate
parts:
Dear all,

I know that the linear predictor can be used as a covariate in other models. Can exp(linear predictor) be used as a covariate?

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] exp(linear predictor) as a covariate
parts:
not in INLA. I think inlabru can handle.

(in most cases do you not want to use exp(lin.pred) as a covariate, but I
presume you know what you're doing...)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] exp(linear predictor) as a covariate
parts:
Hi Håvard, 

Thank you for your response.  I considered using the log-transformed combined spatial field from a hurdle model (logit-link binomial and log-link gamma) as a covariate, but it seems complicated. I think that instead of using a hurdle model, I can use the Tweedie distribution to obtain a single spatial field.

Thanks,
Ruby
